description: Reference choreography from the @gavvanwie TikTok (15.0 s of content; the 19 s clip ends with a 4 s TikTok end card). Hallway duo, knee-up framing; main dancer = tracker id 2 (dark t-shirt, screen left at the start, swaps to screen right at about 12 s). Move boundaries from the wrist/elbow trajectories, hip x (travel) and upper-body motion energy of data/dance/pose/gavvanwie_e42691.npz (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema).

moves.name: Ready: standing, arms hanging and swinging gently out to the sides and together at the hips
Arms spread wide and rise to chest height, then the hands clap together at the chest
Both hands bounce up and down together in front of the waist and chest, dipping toward screen left
Hands keep bouncing at the waist, shifted toward screen right with the body leaning that way
Arms drop to the sides, screen-left leg kicks out, then step to screen left turning to face the partner, short pause
Screen-right arm reaches forward to tap the partner's hand at waist height, then swings up overhead into a high five
Screen-right arm held straight up, hand pressed against the partner's hand overhead
Walk across to screen right past the partner, the raised arm lowering to shoulder height and then down to the side
Both hands sweep together side to side at the waist (left, right, left), then rise to shoulder height and drop to the hips

notes: Reference ankles are NaN in 78% of ok frames and knees in 11-16%: the 'legs' fault rarely fires on this dance and the kick at about 7.5 s is only weakly captured by the pose data.
'ready' is the count-in: the judge's reference clock starts count_in_s after the first ok learner frame unless set_ref_clock is used.
Dancer is present (ok=True) in frames 0-449 only; frames 450-569 are the TikTok end card, so the last move ends at the last ok frame (449, t=14.966 s).
Hand-roll cycle in hand_roll_left/right is about 0.91 s per up-down (wrist peaks at 3.83, 4.77, 5.70, 6.57 s); bpm left null because it is unclear whether that is one or two beats of the track.

The dancers swap sides during walk_across (reference hip x goes from 0.16 to 0.77 of the frame width between 11.5 and 12.7 s) and the camera pans; the reference's absolute screen position is not meaningful from 8 s on.
The npz 'left_wrist'/'left_elbow' (idx 9/7) are the dancer's screen-right arm (mirrored clip); move names use screen sides, which match the learner's own sides when mirroring the screen.
